title: Foreground a choice or report an arrangement

variants.label: ことにする · deliberate choice

segments.role: ことにする foregrounds choosing a course of action; しました places that decision in the past. It can also express a shared decision, so the chooser is not always one individual. The choice does not by itself prove that attendance has happened.

example.translation: I decided to attend next week’s meeting online.
example.note: You are explaining the choice you made about attendance.

variants.change: ことにする foregrounds choosing a course of action; しました places that decision in the past. It can also express a shared decision, so the chooser is not always one individual. The choice does not by itself prove that attendance has happened.

variants.label: ことになる · arranged outcome

segments.role: ことになる presents the arrangement as an established outcome while leaving the decision-maker in the background. The speaker may have helped decide it; this form does not mean that an outside authority always made the choice, or that it happened by chance.

example.translation: It has been arranged that I will attend next week’s meeting online.
example.note: You are reporting the attendance arrangement now in place.

variants.change: ことになる presents the arrangement as an established outcome while leaving the decision-maker in the background. The speaker may have helped decide it; this form does not mean that an outside authority always made the choice, or that it happened by chance.

question: You want to emphasize your own deliberate choice about how to attend. Which ending foregrounds choosing?
answers: 参加することにしました。
参加することになりました。
feedback: ことにしました foregrounds the decision to act. ことになりました reports the resulting arrangement while backgrounding who decided; it can still describe an arrangement you helped make.
